assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a rare complete arc from hormone discovery to transformative medicines: GLP-1 as an insulinotropic hormone, its biological actions and short half-life, and long-acting agonists that now treat type 2 diabetes and obesity with documented cardiometabolic benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact on a major chronic disease are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established the physiology and therapeutic rationale over decades; Mojsov's early identification of the active GLP-1 peptide form is an important and contested contribution. Knudsen led liraglutide/semaglutide development in industry, and other pioneers are not in the credited list, so a three-person configuration necessarily omits significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy is confirmed in large independent randomized trials and real-world data over more than a decade; the science is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between hormone discovery and drug development (Knudsen) is unresolved.
Mojsov's priority relative to others is disputed; I cannot independently verify the details.
Long-term safety and durability of obesity treatment are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of kinase-inhibitor oncology. Concept, compound and clinical proof are all clear and of lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio; credit is comparatively clean, though other medicinal chemists and earlier BCR-ABL work contributed.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of survival data and multiple independent confirmations; recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Industrial chemistry contributors beyond Lydon may merit consideration.
Sawyers' role (resistance, second-generation drugs) could be weighed differently from the original proof of principle.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that its blockade gives clinical benefit in rheumatoid arthritis opened the biologic era in autoimmune and inflammatory disease, with downstream use in Crohn's disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthropathies. Mechanistic insight and patient impact are both profound.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are the natural pair for the translational concept (cytokine cascade and the first clinical trials); antibody engineering and cytokine discovery contributions of others fall outside the supplied credit, so the configuration may be seen as incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of clinical experience, many independent trials and biosimilars; the interpretation is stable and recognition is well past mature.
uncertainties: Credit relative to antibody engineering and TNF cloning work outside the supplied list is unresolved.
Whether the committee treats this as a clinical advance or a discovery is a matter of judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, and population data show large declines in HPV-related disease; the work builds on the already recognized causal role of HPV in cervical cancer. A clear, original technology with major global public-health impact.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLP self-assembly; Frazer and collaborators developed VLP expression in parallel, and others also contributed. A three-person configuration is plausible but not uncontested, and the credited list limits the choices.
assessment.maturity: Large randomized trials and national registry evidence confirm reduction of cervical disease; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority among parallel VLP developments, including contributors not in the list, is a recognized allocation problem.
Long-term cancer-endpoint data are still accumulating in some populations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality; the concept of redirecting immunity is original and the impact is substantial and growing, including toward autoimmune disease.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June developed second-generation CAR designs and the first successful clinical programs; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early engineered T-cell trials. The foundational chimeric-receptor concept of others is not in the credited list, so the configuration is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products with multi-year follow-up; benefit in solid tumors remains limited and toxicity persists, so recognition may be somewhat early outside hematologic cancer.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept is not captured by the supplied names.
Durability and toxicity are still evolving, and solid-tumor efficacy is unproven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted into type I interferon and inflammatory responses, with broad relevance to infection, autoimmunity (interferonopathies, lupus-related biology), cancer immunity and senescence. Conceptually fundamental and clearly original.
assessment.attribution: Chen is credited with cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger; Barber and Ishikawa with STING. Sun and Wu were co-authors of the cGAS/cGAMP work. A Chen plus Barber-led configuration looks most defensible, though the allocation among contributors is uncertain to me.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistic findings are widely reproduced and accepted; clinical translation is not yet established, so recognition rests on basic discovery.
uncertainties: Therapeutic payoff of pathway modulation is not yet demonstrated.
Allocation among Chen's co-authors and Barber/Ishikawa should be checked against primary literature, which I have not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) produced the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, transforming a lethal pediatric disease and validating splice-switching oligonucleotides as a drug class.
assessment.attribution: Krainer contributed the splicing mechanism and target identification, Bennett the oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development; the pairing is coherent, though SMN gene discoverers and other splicing researchers contributed to the foundations.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of clinical follow-up; competing modalities complicate the landscape but do not weaken the discovery.
uncertainties: Contribution of SMN gene discovery and alternative SMN2-targeting approaches to the allocation of credit is unclear.
Long-term outcomes across age ranges are still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of cell-free fetal DNA in maternal plasma created noninvasive prenatal testing, now widely used, and extended into liquid biopsy for cancer; a clear originating discovery with large clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Lo is the clear originator of the maternal-plasma fetal DNA finding and its diagnostic development, supporting a single-laureate configuration; later sequencing-based advances involved others who would not be credited.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation and extensive clinical validation, including population-scale screening; recognition is timely, though the work is closer to diagnostic technology than fundamental physiology.
uncertainties: Whether the committee weighs diagnostic advances equally with mechanistic discoveries is uncertain.
False-positive and interpretation issues for some screened conditions remain.
